🪔 The Sacred Journey

From Sacred Cow
to Your Kitchen

Every jar carries the memory of open farmlands, patient hands, and a ritual that begins before the sun rises. This is not just ghee — this is a 5,000-year-old act of love.

01
🐄
Step 01 · The Cow
Free-Roaming A2 Desi Cows of Bayalu Seeme
Our indigenous Hallikar & Desi cows roam the open plains of Bayalu Seeme, Karnataka. Never confined, never stressed, never injected. Their A2 milk carries the memory of open grasslands — rich, pure, and alive.
🌅 At dawn · Every morning
02
🥛
Step 02 · The Curd
Overnight Curd Setting — Slow & Probiotic-Rich
Fresh warm milk is cultured with a spoonful of the previous day's curd — a living gift passed down generations. By morning, it has transformed into thick, probiotic-rich dahi with deep natural flavour.
🌙 Overnight · 8–10 hours
03
🪔
Step 03 · The Bilona
Hand-Churned at Dawn with a Wooden Bilona
Before sunrise, the curd is hand-churned using a traditional wooden bilona — rotating it both ways, as tradition demands. This sacred motion separates pure butter while preserving every ounce of butyric acid, omega-3s, and vitamins. No machine can replicate this.
🌄 Pre-dawn · 45 minutes of love
04
🔥
Step 04 · The Fire
Slow-Cooked on a Wood Fire — Exactly as Grandma Did
The hand-churned butter is placed in a thick earthen pot and cooked over a gentle wood fire. As the milk solids caramelise and rise, the ghee transforms — deepening in colour, releasing a deep nutty aroma that fills the kitchen with warmth. This is the moment of transformation.
🌿 Low & slow · 2–3 hours
05
✨
Step 05 · The Seal
Hand-Filled. No Machines. Sealed with Gratitude.
The liquid gold is strained through a clean cloth, cooled naturally, and poured by hand into glass jars. No machines touch it. No preservatives enter it. Just pure ghee — the same jar that might sit on your grandmother's shelf — ready to carry tradition into your home.
🏺 Small batch · Always fresh
